pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: The Gingerbread Man
work.note: The Gingerbread Man é um conto popular de tradição oral, registrado em versões impressas em inglês no século XIX, sem autor conhecido. Um casal faz um biscoito de gengibre em forma de boneco. O biscoito ganha vida, foge do forno e corre, desafiando todos que querem comê-lo. A referência abre a situação para praticar “dizer do que gosta (I like) e do que não gosta (I don’t like) usando adjetivos de sabor e textura”.

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

compare.us: In the USA breakfast can be eggs, toast, cereal or pancakes, with coffee or juice. People often say “I like it with milk.”
compare.tip: Say I like it. Do not forget it: “I like it,” not “I like.”

pages.title: Breakfast with my friend Malik · 1/3
paragraphs: My name is Fatima, and I live in **Dearborn**. Every Saturday I have breakfast with my friend Malik. We always go to the same small diner.

“**Do you like** coffee?” Malik asked me last week. “Yes, I do. I like it with milk,” I said. “And tea?” “**No, I don’t**. I like coffee.” He laughed. “**To each their own**,” he said. He likes tea with honey.
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Breakfast with my friend Malik · 2/3
paragraphs: The waiter asked, “What do you like for breakfast?” “I like eggs and toast,” I said. “**Me too**! I love eggs,” said Malik. He also asked for hot sauce. “**I’m not a fan** of spicy food,” I said, “but it’s **my thing** when it is a little sweet!” I do not like it very hot. For Malik, spicy is **his thing**. For me, it is **not my thing**.

That makes me think of the story of the Gingerbread Man. A woman makes a cookie, and he jumps out of the oven. He runs away and says, “Run, run, as fast as you can! You can’t catch me!” He is spicy and sweet, and everybody wants to eat him. “**Yum**!” says the fox in the end.

pages.title: Breakfast with my friend Malik · 3/3
paragraphs: We finished our eggs and toast. “**I like spicy food**, but not too much,” Malik said. We always eat together on Saturday. It is my favorite day of the week.
